summary.headline: Kaynes Q2 FY27 revenue INR9,525 mn (EBITDA margin 13.2%), with Smart Meter revenue down ~80% as the company prioritised balance-sheet repair.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR9,525 mn with EBITDA of INR1,256 mn (13.2% margin) and PAT of INR398 mn; H1 revenue was INR18,987 mn with 14.1% EBITDA margin. Management deliberately cut Smart Meter revenue to cut receivables, while core EMS grew about 34% YoY. Q2 results followed a restatement under Ind AS 8 with new auditor Walker Chandiok & Co, which moved bill discounting into borrowings and restated FY26 PAT to INR392 crore from INR364 crore. Management also announced a Vishay partnership in Kaynes Semicon (49% stake, term sheet only) and an acquisition of the Toyokawa JV for TFT display modules.

financial_highlights.value: INR221 crore (Semicon INR59 crore, Circuits INR140 crore, EMS INR21 crore)

segments.name: EMS (ex-metering)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR799 crore, up 34% YoY; management says EMS margin was about 10.5% last year, and H1 blended EBITDA is 14.1% with metering at about 10% of revenue. Management targets >30% EMS growth in FY27.

segments.name: Smart Metering
segments.commentary: Revenue deliberately moderated: down about 12% in Q1 and about 80% in Q2; H1 revenue about INR270 crore vs about INR960 crore in FY26. Management is seeking a partner for a deal with the manufacturing kept in-house and installation/O&M handed to a third party, with a plan promised by next quarter-end.

segments.name: Aerospace and railways
segments.commentary: Management says these segments grew more than 50% (aerospace more than 70%) and are high-margin; Kavach product approved and eligible for commercial production.

segments.name: OSAT and PCB (Kaynes Semicon and Kaynes Circuits)
segments.commentary: Unit 2 of both now operational with multiple products under customer approval; PCB Unit 1 to start revenue in Q3 FY27, with both moving to full operation by Q4. Vishay to take 75-90% of Semicon capacity.

segments.name: August Electronics (North America)
segments.commentary: Growth below expectations due to global conflicts; export revenue share targeted from about 10% to 25%+ by 2030 under Mission 30.

guidance_outlook: Management reiterated confidence of more than 30% EMS (electronics) growth for FY27 and growth of roughly double the market rate (market growing above 15%).
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger in revenue and margin, with OSAT/PCB revenue from Q3 and full operation by Q4.
Margins expected to normalise over coming quarters as commodity and crude-linked costs ease; management says the metering-exit margin gap can be recovered via VAVE and productivity gains.
Smart Meter revenue in H2 depends on collections; management targets bringing receivables below INR750 crore before additional sales.
Management says no QIP for at least one year; funding expected from Vishay-linked dilution and inventory release (about INR250 crore strategic inventory to be eased from December).
capex_capacity: Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuits became operational in Q2/Q3 FY27; PCB Unit 1 revenue from Q3 FY27.

Vishay partnership: initial agreement signed, term sheet stage; Vishay to take 75-90% of Semicon capacity, with the rest kept for existing validated customers; definitive agreement expected in 2-3 months.
Vishay 49% stake to sit at Kaynes Semicon level for now; separate subsidiary or SPV not yet decided; Kaynes to retain 51% control.
Net working-capital inventory held at about INR150 crore for strategic reasons; management plans to ease it from end-December if supply conditions normalise.
Toyokawa JV acquired for entry into TFT display modules for vehicle electronics.
demand_pricing: Core EMS demand strong; management expects EMS revenue to keep growing even without metering.
PCB is globally short with lead times of 6-8 months and advance payments requested by suppliers; engagement with a large global EV manufacturer ongoing.
Commodity costs elevated: copper and aluminium at multi-year highs, wholesale inflation near 10%, manufactured product inflation 8.4%.
Rupee moved from about INR85 (June 2025) to INR95-96, with recent RBI measures bringing it back to about INR95; Brent moved above $100 in September.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vishay capacity dedicated or incremental, and are existing contracts shrinking?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishay capacity comes from existing built capacity; 75-90% goes to Vishay and 10-25% is retained for existing customers. Management says existing commitments are not reducing.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables move into borrowings and what is the restatement?
qa_highlights.answer: Bill discounting, previously a separate line, is now shown in borrowings. Restatement moved West Bengal metering to a service concession model (revenue up INR41.8 crore) and corrected timing and inventory provision errors; FY26 EBITDA moved from 15.8% to 14.2%.

qa_highlights.question: Smart Meter FY27 and FY28 revenue and receivable outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 Smart Meter revenue about INR270 crore; H2 depends on collections, with a receivable target below INR750 crore before more sales. Management says installation is slow and government clearances are pending.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vishay investment fund ISM or other commitments, and will there be fund raising?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishay proceeds will repay the parent company's loan; management says it will not go to market for a QIP for the next year.

qa_highlights.question: Smart Meter exit structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing stays in-house; installation and O&M to be given to a third party with first right to buy; plan promised by next quarter-end (February).

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says capex is being kept prudent: incremental Q2 capex about INR221 crore net of subsidy, split across Semicon (INR59 crore net), Circuits (INR140 crore) and EMS (INR21 crore).

risks_watch: Restatement under Ind AS 8 (FY26 PAT to INR392 crore from INR364 crore) with an emphasis-of-matter paragraph in limited review reports; monitor audit trail and presentation.
Smart Meter receivables at INR1,091 crore; collections and government installation pace are gating factors for any H2 revenue.
OSAT/PCB ramp and end-product validation; management flagged this as the open item, with timelines already slipping by a couple of quarters.
Vishay definitive agreement (2-3 months) and the structure at Kaynes Semicon level remain undefined; a separate Smart Meter partner deal is still pending.
Working capital at 169 days, up from 163; inventory build of INR200-250 crore to be released only if supply chains normalise.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and EMS growth but cautious on near-term numbers: management openly acknowledged deliberate revenue cuts and margin pressure. Responses were often lengthy and repetitive, with several evasive points on Vishay structure, Smart Meter deal terms and the restatement details.
key_quotes: This quarter, we choose to put balance sheet strength and cash discipline ahead of short-term revenue, while continuing to invest ahead of time in the capabilities that will define Kaynes over the next decade.
Vishay will take up about 75%-90% of the capacity, which gives us a direct access to the global market other than China.
we are very, very confident that we are not going to go to the market for the money.

growth.why: Management reiterates >30% EMS growth for FY27 and revenue growth of about double the market rate, with H2 stronger; backing is partial: Semicon Unit 2 and Circuits Unit 2 are operational, PCB Unit 1 revenue starts Q3 FY27, the INR105,635 mn order book is cited, but Smart Meter revenue fell ~80% in Q2 and receivables targets slipped.

oneOffs.what: Smart Meter revenue fell to INR54 crore from INR228 crore a year earlier (about -80%) as management deliberately cut metering to reduce receivables; this drags headline growth, but it is a strategic c

quality.why: Core EMS (ex-metering) revenue rose about 34% YoY to INR799 crore from INR595 crore, which is the recurring driver, while Smart Meter revenue fell about 80% from INR228 crore to INR54 crore by management's choice, so headline Q2 growth is weighed down rather than flattered; no quarter-specific one-off gain or low base is disclosed, and the brief gives no consolidated Q2 revenue growth figure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects margins to normalise as commodity costs ease, but H1 EBITDA margin is 14.1% vs 14.2% restated FY26 and Q2 is 13.2%, with copper and aluminium at multi-year highs and wholesale inflation near 10%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kaynes Semicon Unit 2 and Kaynes Circuits Unit 2 are already operational, and PCB Unit 1 revenue starts Q3 FY27 with both units at full operation by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Core EMS revenue grew 34% YoY to INR799 crore in Q2 and management targets more than 30% EMS growth for FY27, with H2 expected stronger, though Smart Meter revenue fell about 80% to INR54 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Incremental Q2 capex was INR221 crore net of subsidy, but management calls capex prudent and no new plant or utilisation figure was given, so a fresh announcement is not clearly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held its guidance of more than 30% EMS growth and double-market revenue growth, while cutting the Smart Meter receivables target, so no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Smart Meter revenue fell about 80% in Q2 to INR54 crore, receivables are INR1,091 crore against a sub-INR750 crore target, and OSAT/PCB timelines have already slipped a couple of quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PCB Unit 1 starts revenue in Q3 FY27 and Kavach is approved for commercial production, while multiple OSAT products are under customer approval.

rows.label: Vishay partnership in Kaynes Semicon (49% stake)
rows.why: Vishay is to take 75-90% of Semicon capacity, but the deal is at term-sheet stage and the structure at Semicon level is still undefined.

rows.label: Smart Meter receivables reduction below INR750 crore
rows.why: Receivables fell to INR1,091 crore from INR1,402 crore in Q1, and H2 Smart Meter sales depend on collections, with a plan due by February.

rows.label: Strategic inventory release (about INR250 crore)
rows.why: Net working capital is 169 days, up from 163, and management plans to ease inventory from end-December only if supply conditions normalise.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term EMS growth and the OSAT/PCB ramp but cautious on near-term margins and Smart Meter collections; analysts pushed on the Vishay structure, Smart Meter exit terms and the Ind AS 8 restatement, and management was often evasive on those points.
